claims.text: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck at 5.5996, 125.0647 (offshore Sarangani, Philippines) on 7 June 2026 at 23:37 UTC, at 35 km depth, generating a maximum tsunami wave of 1.93 metres; GDACS issued an orange alert for medium humanitarian impact with about 2.9 million people exposed to Modified Mercalli Intensity VII or greater.

OCHA's 'Philippines: 7.8 Sarangani Earthquake Response Snapshot' (as of 13 July 2026) reports 94 deaths, 1,316 injured and 18 missing, alongside 391,891 families (1,655,313 persons) affected across 650 barangays and 25,048 families (95,629 persons) still displaced.

DSWD DROMIC Report #75, as of 23 July 2026, 6PM, reports 392,157 families (1,656,596 persons) affected across 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM (Tulunan, North Cotabato added: 10 barangays, 182 families). Total displaced: 27,118 families (107,475 persons) — 7,592 families (30,889 persons) inside 75 evacuation centers, 19,526 families (76,586 persons) outside with relatives/friends. Houses damaged: 115,205 total (18,644 totally destroyed, 96,561 partially damaged) — revised down from prior reports after data validation and deduplication conducted 21 July 2026. Cost of assistance provided to date: PHP 1,288,971,829.87.

DSWD DROMIC Report #76, as of 24 July 2026, 6PM, reports a total of 392,389 families (1,657,524 persons) affected in 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM. There are 7,982 families (32,890 persons) currently taking temporary shelter in 85 evacuation centers in Regions XI and XII, and 19,526 families (76,555 persons) temporarily staying with relatives or friends; total displaced stands at 27,508 families (109,445 persons) in Regions XI, XII and BARMM. A total of 115,205 houses were damaged, of which 18,644 were totally damaged and 96,561 were partially damaged, in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM. A total of ₱1,306,112,420.37 worth of assistance was provided to the affected families, of which ₱1,306,092,420.37 from DSWD and ₱20,000.00 from the LGUs.

DSWD DROMIC Report #77, as of 31 July 2026, 6PM (published on ReliefWeb 3 August 2026), reports 392,389 families (1,657,524 persons) affected across 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM (unchanged from Report #76). Total displaced: 27,289 families (108,472 persons) -- 7,763 families (31,917 persons) inside 86 evacuation centers (up from 85) and 19,526 families (76,555 persons) staying outside with relatives or friends. Houses damaged: 115,205 total (18,644 totally destroyed, 96,561 partially damaged), unchanged from Report #76. Cost of assistance provided to date: PHP 1,383,697,520.37 (PHP 1,383,677,520.37 from DSWD and PHP 20,000.00 from LGUs), up from PHP 1,306,112,420.37 in Report #76. The report's casualty section still does not carry a death/injured/missing figure.

DSWD DROMIC Report #78 (as of 6 August 2026, 6PM) reports 392,389 families (1,657,524 persons) affected across 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM (unchanged from Report #77). Total displacement eased slightly to 27,244 families (108,272 persons) -- 7,718 families (31,717 persons) in 86 evacuation centers and 19,526 families (76,555 persons) staying outside with relatives or friends -- down from 27,289 families (108,472 persons) in Report #77. Houses damaged remain unchanged at 115,205 total (18,644 totally destroyed, 96,561 partially damaged). Assistance provided to date rose to PHP 1,410,517,316.87. DSWD's DROMIC template still carries no casualty section; the freshest citable casualty figure remains OCHA's 13 July 2026 snapshot (94 deaths, 1,316 injured, 18 missing).

Re-checked 8 August 2026: DSWD DROMIC Report #78 (6 August 2026, 6PM) remains the latest in its series on ReliefWeb; the OCHA 13 July casualty snapshot (94 deaths, 1,316 injured, 18 missing) remains the freshest citable casualty figure. Separately, USGS recorded a new M6.3 aftershock on 5 August 2026 at 04:14 UTC, 32 km SW of Sarangani, Philippines (10 km depth, Green alert, no tsunami warning) -- part of the same aftershock sequence PHIVOLCS has been tracking since the 8 June mainshock; no allowlisted source has reported new casualties or damage from this aftershock.

At least 19 people were killed, 12 remain missing and at least 134 were injured after the 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck Sarangani province on 8 June 2026, according to OCHA, with authorities noting the figures were provisional as assessments continued; more than 3.2 million learners were affected with classes suspended in over 6,200 schools.

USGS recorded a new M5.1 aftershock on 5 August 2026 at 05:59:21 UTC, 46 km SSW of Sarangani, Philippines, at a depth of about 29.8 km, with no tsunami generated and no alert issued — part of the same aftershock sequence PHIVOLCS has tracked since the 8 June 2026 mainshock.

Re-checked 11 August 2026: reliefweb.int, this record's live_source_url and the source of the DSWD DROMIC series and OCHA casualty snapshot, returned HTTP 403 Forbidden and was unreachable across multiple attempts and multiple pages (disaster hub, specific report URLs, API endpoint) today. As an alternate allowlisted check, GDACS's report page for this event was fetched and remains active with an Orange alert ("medium humanitarian impact"), currently showing modeled population exposure of about 4.4 million people at MMI≥VII and a maximum observed tsunami wave of 0.83 m -- GDACS's own automated impact-model figures for the event, which are updated as GDACS reprocesses episodes and are distinct from the ground-assessed OCHA casualty snapshot (94 deaths) and DSWD displacement/housing figures already on file; they do not supersede those confirmed figures. No new confirmed casualty or displacement figure was found via any accessible allowlisted source.

DSWD DROMIC Report #79 (as of 14 August 2026, 6AM): 392,506 families (1,661,828 persons) affected in 661 barangays across Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM; 27,029 families (107,197 persons) remain displaced (7,503 families/30,642 persons in 80 evacuation centres, 19,526 families/76,555 persons staying with relatives/friends); 138,563 houses damaged (19,320 totally, 119,243 partially); PHP 1,453,887,143.87 worth of assistance provided to date. DROMIC reports do not carry casualty figures; no allowlisted source has updated the death toll beyond OCHA's earlier count.

DSWD DROMIC Report #80 (as of 21 August 2026, 6AM): 392,506 families (1,661,828 persons) remain affected across 661 barangays, unchanged from Report #79. Total displaced eased to 26,422 families (105,558 persons) -- 7,058 families (29,033 persons) in 80 evacuation centres and 19,364 families (76,525 persons) staying with relatives or friends -- down from 27,029 families (107,197 persons) in Report #79. Houses damaged remain unchanged at 138,563 total (19,320 totally, 119,243 partially damaged). Assistance provided to date rose to PHP 1,496,461,207.87.

By 23 June, government figures reported 77 deaths, with about 1.6 million people affected across Regions IX, XI, XII, and BARMM. PHIVOLCS recorded more than 9,400 aftershocks and further seismic activity expected. More than 80,000 houses have been damaged, including nearly 15,000 destroyed, with 884 damaged infrastructure losses and 130 affected roads and 47 bridges limiting access to isolated communities. Eighteen local government units (LGUs) have declared a state of calamity.

DSWD DROMIC Report #58, as of 09 July 2026, 6AM, reports 391,891 families (1,655,313 persons) affected in 650 barangays across Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM, with 24,097 families (92,256 persons) still displaced — 7,008 families (28,090 persons) inside 74 evacuation centers and 17,089 families (64,166 persons) staying outside evacuation centers with relatives or friends. A total of 121,426 houses were damaged, of which 19,305 were totally destroyed and 102,121 partially damaged.

There are 25,048 families (95,629 persons) still displaced in Regions XI, XII and BARMM — 7,959 families (31,463 persons) inside 80 evacuation centers in Regions XI and XII, and 17,089 families (64,166 persons) temporarily staying with relatives or friends. DSWD DROMIC Report #72, as of 20 July 2026, 6PM, reports 391,975 families (1,655,686 persons) affected across 651 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM (unchanged from Report #71). Total displaced: 24,640 families (94,559 persons) — 7,551 families (30,393 persons) inside 75 evacuation centers, 17,089 families (64,166 persons) outside with relatives/friends. description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck offshore Sarangani province in the southern Philippines on 8 June 2026 (7 June 23:37 UTC), generating a tsunami and widespread damage across Mindanao; GDACS maintains an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact, its reprocessed model showing about 4.4 million people exposed to MMI VII or greater and a maximum observed tsunami wave of 0.83 metres. OCHA's response snapshot of 13 July 2026 recorded 94 deaths, 1,316 injured and 18 missing — still the standing official casualty count, as DSWD's DROMIC reporting series does not carry casualty figures — and eighteen local government units have declared a state of calamity. Per DSWD DROMIC Report #79 (as of 14 August 2026), 392,506 families (1,661,828 persons) are affected across 661 barangays in Regions IX, XI, XII and BARMM, 26,422 families (105,558 persons) remain displaced, and 138,563 houses have been damaged (19,320 totally, 119,243 partially). Aftershocks, including a magnitude 6.3 shock on 5 August 2026, have continued as the humanitarian response goes on.

updates.text: DSWD DROMIC Report #80 (21 August, 6AM) recorded displacement easing to 26,422 families (105,558 persons), down from 27,029 families (107,197 persons); affected population (392,506 families) and damaged houses (138,563) held unchanged; assistance provided rose to PHP 1,496,461,207.87. OCHA's 13 July toll (94 deaths, 1,316 injured, 18 missing) remains the freshest confirmed figure.

DSWD DROMIC Report #79 (as of 14 August, 6AM) put the affected population at 392,506 families (1,661,828 persons), displacement at 27,029 families (107,197 persons) and damaged houses at 138,563 (19,320 totally, 119,243 partially) — the housing-damage total revised up from 115,205 — with assistance provided reaching PHP 1,453,887,143.87.

GDACS's reprocessed impact model for the event now shows about 4.4 million people exposed to MMI VII or greater and a maximum observed tsunami wave of 0.83 metres, versus the roughly 2.9 million exposure and 1.93-metre maximum modelled at the outset; the ground-assessed OCHA casualty and DSWD displacement figures are unaffected.

DSWD DROMIC Report #78 (as of 6 August, 6PM) recorded displacement easing to 27,244 families (108,272 persons) from 27,289 families (108,472 persons) in Report #77, with houses damaged unchanged at 115,205 and assistance provided rising to PHP 1,410,517,316.87.

USGS recorded M6.3 and M5.1 aftershocks on 5 August 2026 — 32 km SW and 46 km SSW of Sarangani respectively — with no tsunami warning and no new casualties or damage reported, part of the aftershock sequence PHIVOLCS has tracked since the 8 June mainshock.

DSWD DROMIC Report #77 (as of 31 July, 6PM) recorded 27,289 families (108,472 persons) displaced across 86 evacuation centres and with relatives, houses damaged unchanged at 115,205, and assistance provided of PHP 1,383,697,520.37; the DROMIC series no longer carries a casualty section, leaving OCHA's 13 July snapshot (94 deaths) as the standing toll.
